findings.documented: API key is sent as a query parameter: ?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: API key must be sent as a request header: X-API-Key: IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX.
findings.how_found: first API call using the documented query parameter method returned an error with explicit instructions to use the header instead
findings.impact: every request must use the X-API-Key header; the documented method fails on all endpoints
evidence: Using a query parameter returns {"detail": "send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter"}

findings.documented: Login response has field 'token', expires_in 86400 (24h), user object contains 'name', and 'there is no refresh flow'
findings.actual: Login response field is 'access_token' (not 'token'), expires_in is 900 (15min), user object has no 'name' field, and a refresh flow exists via 'refresh_token'
findings.how_found: called POST /auth/login and compared the actual response structure against the documented one, then tested POST /auth/refresh with the returned refresh_token
findings.impact: frontend must use 'access_token' field, implement token refresh every 15 minutes via /auth/refresh, and cannot rely on a user 'name' field

findings.documented: POST /auth/logout invalidates the current token server side
findings.actual: Tokens are stateless and discarded on client side. Discarded tokens remain valid until expiry (15 min) and refresh tokens until their expiry (7 days), even after logout is called
findings.how_found: called POST /auth/logout, observed the response note about stateless tokens, then verified by using the 'discarded' access_token on GET /v1/listings (still worked), waiting for access_token expiry, and using the 'discarded' refresh_token on POST /auth/refresh (still generated new tokens)
findings.impact: logout is client-side only — clear tokens from storage. No server-side revocation exists. Refresh tokens remain usable for 7 days from issue regardless of logout
evidence: Logout returns {"ok": true, "note": "tokens are stateless; discard them client side"}
